title: Exergy — A Measure of Work Potential
source: Cengel, Boles & Kanoglu — Thermodynamics: An Engineering Approach, Ch. 8
summary:
The first law counts energy; the second law judges its **quality**. **Exergy** (also called *availability*) puts a number on that quality: it is the **maximum useful work** that can be obtained from a system as it comes to equilibrium with its environment through *reversible* processes. Energy is conserved, but exergy is not — every real process **destroys** some of it. Exergy analysis is how engineers find *where* work potential is being wasted.

Everything is measured relative to the **dead state**: the environment's temperature and pressure $T_0, P_0$ (often 25 °C, 1 atm). A system in equilibrium with the dead state has zero exergy — it can do no more useful work, even if it still holds plenty of energy. This is why a vast lake of lukewarm water has enormous internal energy but almost no exergy.

Different energy forms carry different exergy. **Work** is entirely exergy (it is already organized, fully usable). **Kinetic and potential energy** are fully exergy too. **Heat**, however, is only partly exergy: heat $Q$ supplied from a reservoir at temperature $T$ carries exergy $(1 - T_0/T)\,Q$ — the Carnot fraction. The hotter the source relative to the environment, the more of its heat can become work; heat at the dead-state temperature carries no exergy at all. For matter, the **flow exergy** of a stream is $\psi = (h - h_0) - T_0(s - s_0) + V^2/2 + gz$, and a closed system has the analogous non-flow exergy $\phi$ with a $P_0(v - v_0)$ term for the work done against the atmosphere.

The central result is the **exergy balance**: exergy in − exergy out − exergy destroyed = change in the system's exergy. The destruction term is always positive for real processes and is tied directly to entropy generation by the **Gouy–Stodola relation**, $X_{dest} = T_0\,S_{gen} \ge 0$. Anywhere entropy is generated — friction, unrestrained expansion, heat transfer across a finite temperature difference, mixing — exergy is irreversibly lost.

Finally, performance is judged by the **second-law (exergy) efficiency** $\eta_{II}$: useful exergy output over exergy supplied. Unlike thermal efficiency, it compares a device to the *reversible ideal* for the same task, so a 40%-efficient power plant might still be 70% efficient in second-law terms. The workflow: pick the dead state, tally the exergy of each stream/heat/work interaction, and either close the balance for the destruction or compute $T_0 S_{gen}$ directly.

equations.name: Exergy of heat transfer
equations.useWhen: Finding the work potential of heat supplied from (or rejected to) a reservoir at temperature $T$. It is the Carnot-weighted part of the heat.
equations.note: $T, T_0$ absolute. Heat at the dead-state temperature ($T = T_0$) carries zero exergy.

equations.name: Flow (stream) exergy
equations.useWhen: Exergy carried by a flowing stream in a control volume (turbines, compressors, heat exchangers). Use the *change* $\Delta\psi$ between inlet and outlet.
equations.note: Subscript 0 = dead state. The $-T_0(s-s_0)$ term is the unavailable part.

equations.name: Closed-system (non-flow) exergy
equations.useWhen: Work potential of a fixed mass relative to the dead state. The $P_0(v - v_0)$ term subtracts work done uselessly against the atmosphere.
equations.note: Per unit mass ($\phi$) or total ($X = m\phi$).

equations.name: Exergy destruction (Gouy–Stodola)
equations.useWhen: The fastest route to wasted work: compute entropy generation, multiply by the dead-state temperature. Works for any process or device.
equations.note: Always $\ge 0$; zero only for reversible processes. Pinpoints *where* exergy is lost.

equations.name: Exergy balance (steady control volume)
equations.useWhen: Accounting for all exergy flows (by heat, work, and mass) across a device to find the destruction or the reversible work.
equations.note: Exergy enters/leaves with heat ($(1-T_0/T)Q$), work ($W$), and mass ($\dot m\psi$); the imbalance is destroyed.

equations.name: Second-law (exergy) efficiency
equations.useWhen: Judging a device against the reversible ideal for the *same task* — a fairer score than first-law efficiency.
equations.note: Ranges 0–1; the gap from 1 is the fraction of supplied exergy destroyed.

glossary.definition: The maximum useful work obtainable from a system as it reversibly reaches equilibrium with the environment. A measure of energy *quality*, not quantity.
Equilibrium with the environment at $T_0, P_0$ (often 25 °C, 1 atm). A system at the dead state has zero exergy.
Work potential of heat from a reservoir at $T$: $(1 - T_0/T)Q$ — the Carnot fraction. Zero when $T = T_0$.
Exergy carried by a flowing stream: $(h - h_0) - T_0(s - s_0) + V^2/2 + gz$.
Exergy of a closed system, including a $P_0(v - v_0)$ term for work done against the atmosphere.
Work potential irreversibly lost, $X_{dest} = T_0 S_{gen} \ge 0$. Caused by every irreversibility.
$X_{dest} = T_0\,S_{gen}$ — links destroyed exergy directly to entropy generation.
The maximum work output (or minimum work input) for a given change of state, achieved with no irreversibilities.
The difference between reversible and actual useful work, $I = W_{rev} - W_u = X_{dest}$.
Useful exergy output over exergy supplied; compares a device to the reversible ideal for the same task.

tips: **Fix the dead state first.** Every exergy term is measured relative to $T_0$ (and $P_0$). Note them at the start and use $T_0$ in all $(1 - T_0/T)$ and $T_0 S_{gen}$ terms — in **kelvin**.
**Fastest destruction route:** find $S_{gen}$ from an entropy balance, then $X_{dest} = T_0 S_{gen}$. Usually quicker than a full exergy balance.
**Heat ≠ exergy.** Only $(1 - T_0/T)$ of a heat input is convertible work potential. High-temperature heat is 'high quality'; near-ambient heat is nearly worthless.
**Work and KE/PE are pure exergy** (100% convertible). Internal/thermal energy is only partly exergy — that asymmetry is the whole point of the chapter.
**$\eta_{II}$ flips for consumers.** Work-*producing* devices: $W_u/W_{rev}$. Work-*consuming* devices (pumps, compressors): $W_{rev}/W_u$. Same idea — useful exergy over what you paid.
**Exergy is destroyed, not transferred away.** A positive $X_{dest}$ is lost forever; it doesn't reappear elsewhere. Minimizing $S_{gen}$ is minimizing this loss.
